annotation.method: Every line in scope was read. A location is POSITIVE iff it names, or binds a name to, a quantum-vulnerable cryptographic primitive in a position that determines the algorithm. A location that merely OPERATES on a primitive chosen elsewhere (cipher.init, md.update, cipher.encryptor(), .digest()) is NEGATIVE in label set L1 and is counted POSITIVE only in sensitivity variant L2, which is reported alongside L1. Comments, imports of non-primitives, PRNGs, IVs/salts, PBKDF parameter objects, key-store container formats and key/block size plumbing are NEGATIVE with a recorded reason.
annotation.independence: Criteria are written from JCA/SSH semantics and never consult engine/scanner.py's rule table. Labels are frozen data; the harness verifies each label's verbatim source line against the pinned corpus and fails loudly on drift rather than re-deriving labels.

corpora.corpus_notes: Real production library, not a constructed benchmark. N NARROW scope: three hand-read files from the ssh/ package (the cipher, MAC and ML-KEM algorithm tables). Chosen because they enumerate the algorithm surface, and because they are the only files in the package that have been read in full. The other 28 non-test files in ssh/ are NOT annotated and NOT scanned. This corpus contains REAL post-quantum code: ssh/mlkem.go implements a hybrid ML-KEM-768 + X25519 SSH key exchange (draft-kampanakis-curdle-ssh-pq-ke-05).
corpora.scan_root_relative: explicit file list: ssh/cipher.go, ssh/mac.go, ssh/mlkem.go

ground_truth.label_kind: hand-annotated line-level ground truth (author of this harness)

annotation.annotated_by: IndraMesh benchmark harness author, by direct reading of every line in scope
annotation.method: A location is POSITIVE in L1 iff it names, or binds a name to, a quantum-vulnerable cryptographic primitive in a position that determines the algorithm: P1 factory call or mode registration, P1b naming a primitive identifier in executable code, P2 a key-spec/hash binding, P3 an import that determines the algorithm downstream, P4 an SSH/OpenSSL algorithm identifier. A line that merely OPERATES on a primitive chosen elsewhere is NEGATIVE in L1 and POSITIVE in L2; the harness reports both.
annotation.deliberate_exclusions: ML-KEM is labelled NEGATIVE, and this is the most consequential judgement in the set. crypto/mlkem is FIPS 203 -- post-quantum, the REMEDY. The criterion asks for quantum-VULNERABLE primitives, so labelling ML-KEM a vulnerability would invert the meaning of the scan. Poly1305 is negative for the narrower reason that it is in neither declared break model in pqtaxonomy.py.
annotation.scope_caveat: THREE files, not the package. The other 28 non-test files under ssh/ were swept but NOT annotated and are NOT scanned. Recall here is relative to these three files only and says nothing about the rest of x/crypto. This is a small corpus: denominators are printed beside every ratio, and the figure should be read as a smoke test of the Go pack, not as a characterisation of Go detection.
annotation.label_corrections: Corrected after the first measurement, in the direction AGAINST the tool: one missed RC4 positive added (which lowers measured precision), two chacha20 read-path positives added (which removes two false positives), and two L1/L2 rows corrected so the L2 variant is not silently identical to L1. The original token sweep was case-sensitive and missed lowercase qualified calls such as `rc4.NewCipher`; the first annotation pass also labelled only one of two structurally identical call sites. A detector that scores well against incomplete labels is not evidence of anything, which is the reason these were found and fixed rather than tuned around.
